issues.quote: Clicking a link asks Caddy for another address.
issues.text: "Caddy" is a tool name not in known_vocab or the prereq summaries. At its first use in section 2 I pause: who is Caddy? Section 5 ("served by Caddy since the HTTP lessons") tells me it is the thing that serves the lab's pages, so I am not stuck, only delayed. Minor because the role is given in context and it is not part of the main idea.
issues.fix: At the first mention in section 2, write "asks Caddy, the lab's web server, for another address".

issues.quote: Without it, a page can still do what the browser has built in: follow a link to another address, change a colour while the pointer is over something, play an animation its CSS describes.
issues.text: The animation is credited to CSS, but the colour change on pointer-over is not credited to anything. I wonder whether the browser does that on its own for every page or only when CSS says so, and so whether CSS is also a kind of behaviour. The next sentence (own logic vs built-in) settles the main idea, so this is small.
issues.fix: Change "change a colour while the pointer is over something" to "change a colour while the pointer is over something, if the CSS says so".

issues.quote: CSS would cover the message only when it were purely a look, but showing it on a click is behaviour that needs code.
issues.text: The wrong-option explanations for b, c and d use "would ... only when ... were", which I had to read twice to parse. The content is right; the grammar slows me down.
issues.fix: Rewrite b/c/d explanations as plain statements, e.g. c: "CSS can style the message, but showing it on a click is behaviour, which needs JavaScript."
